items.title: Medical Image Segmentation: Foundation Model Adaptation versus Task-Specific Training
items.description: Foundation models pretrained on large natural-image collections are increasingly adapted for medical image segmentation, in the expectation that they will replace models trained for each task. Most comparisons, however, use data from the training distribution and a single task-specific baseline whose configuration is rarely justified, and therefore provide limited evidence of performance at new clinical sites. items.name: TorchCurves: Differentiable Parametric Curves
items.title: TorchCurves: Differentiable Parametric Curves
items.description: We present TorchCurves, a PyTorch library that treats vector-valued parametric curves as learnable primitives. Its central operation maps batches of scalar inputs to points on curves represented in B-spline or Legendre polynomial bases, with differentiation through both inputs and coefficients. Curve coefficients can be optimized jointly with the surrounding model or produced by another network. items.name: AutoScaffold: AI-Guided Scaffolding for Reinforcement Learning of Language Models
items.title: AutoScaffold: AI-Guided Scaffolding for Reinforcement Learning of Language Models
items.description: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) produces rich training experience, yet outcome rewards reduce each attempt to a single number and leave most of this information unused. Training-time scaffolds, such as strategies or hints added to the prompt during training, offer a natural way to turn this information into guidance, but their design and adaptation are largely left to humans and tailored to specific domains. items.name: Contrastive Discovery: Open-Ended Scientific Discovery over Competing Explanations
items.title: Contrastive Discovery: Open-Ended Scientific Discovery over Competing Explanations
items.description: LLM agents are increasingly used for open-ended, data-driven scientific discovery, yet most of them evaluate hypotheses pointwise, testing an empirical claim $h$ only against its complement $\neg h$. When evidence rejects $h$, the agent learns that one explanation is unlikely but not which alternative the evidence supports. items.name: Pyrite: Building and Benchmarking Protein-Ligand Pose Ranking Agents
items.title: Pyrite: Building and Benchmarking Protein-Ligand Pose Ranking Agents
items.description: Predicting how a ligand binds to its target is central to small-molecule drug discovery. Modern cofolding models can generate diverse candidate poses, but reliably ranking these candidates remains challenging. We introduce Pyrite, a pairwise pose-ranking benchmark comprising 1,500 pose pairs across diverse protein-ligand complexes. items.title: When Does the Real Wiring Win? Testing connectome structure-function claims against unmeasured physiology
items.description: Connectome-constrained models are often used to argue that a measured wiring diagram outperforms shuffled or rewired wiring, and hence that structure shapes function. items.title: Continual-ARC: Measuring Skill Acquisition over a Working Lifetime
items.description: Agent harnesses have emerged as a promising mechanism for continual learning, alongside test-time parametric learning. However, the current benchmarks have several limitations: they generally focus on a single applied domain, serve each instance only once, and assume a single family of learner, so memory-based and weight-based systems are rarely compared on the same scale. items.title: Emergent Biological Capabilities in a Foundation Model for Molecular Interactions
items.description: Foundation models trained on large unlabeled corpora develop emergent capabilities, tasks that go beyond the training objective. We extend this paradigm to multimodal biology with Bonbon, a foundation model for molecular interactions trained on approximately 3.2 trillion tokens of paired protein-ligand sequences. items.title: Comparative Analysis of Agent Evaluation Frameworks: Stability, Detection, and Discovery in Enterprise Analytics Agents
items.description: Deploying LLM-based analytics agents in enterprise settings requires evaluation frameworks that can reliably detect failures across complex, multi-tool workflows. We present a three-phase comparative study of three evaluation frameworks, each representing a distinct evaluation paradigm (trace-based LLM judging, text-only LLM judging with red-teaming, and deterministic heuristics), applied to two analytics agents in a controlled research setting using frozen execution traces. items.name: ReTrace: Distilling Tool-Using Agents into Planner-Free Workflows
items.title: ReTrace: Distilling Tool-Using Agents into Planner-Free Workflows
items.description: Business process automation runs the same Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) again and again on new inputs. Large Language Model (LLM) agents can follow an SOP written in natural language, but they call an LLM to choose every step of every run, which adds latency and cost at scale. We present ReTrace, which turns an SOP and a few logged agent runs into a reusable workflow in which code, not an LLM, selects the next step. items.title: TimeSeek: Multi-Task and Multi-Domain Pretraining for Generalized Time Series Analytics
items.description: Time series analytics has been widely applied across various domains. items.name: Re-Search: Dissecting LLM Ideation Through a Two-Player Questioning Game
items.title: Re-Search: Dissecting LLM Ideation Through a Two-Player Questioning Game
items.description: Research ideation is iterative: researchers refine their ideas step by step based on feedback. Yet existing evaluations obscure this search process, making it difficult to understand how LLMs explore the space of research ideas and what limits their progress. We introduce Re-Search, which adapts the format of Twenty Questions to research ideation: given only the research problem of a published paper, a model must rediscover the paper's core idea by asking yes-or-no questions. items.name: Mechanistic Interpretability Needs a Logic of Inference
items.title: Mechanistic Interpretability Needs a Logic of Inference
items.description: Neural networks are increasingly studied not merely as predictive systems, but as complex systems whose internal computations are themselves objects of scientific inquiry. Recent progress in mechanistic interpretability (MI) has made it possible to identify neurons, features, circuits, population structures, and dynamical patterns associated with model behavior. items.name: Pterodactyl: Pushing the Limits of Efficient Automated Translation Evaluation
items.title: Pterodactyl: Pushing the Limits of Efficient Automated Translation Evaluation
items.description: In this paper, we present 1020 Group's submission to the WMT26 shared task on automated quality evaluation. Our system, Pterodactyl, was engineered specifically for subtasks 2 and 3, that is, segment-level quality score prediction and the detection of error-free segments. Pterodactyl is a highly customizable, ultra-low cost system optimized for binary classification in translation triage and data curation. items.name: FERN: Cross-Benchmark Table Retrieval for Text-to-SQL with Frozen Retrievers and Learned Ranking
items.title: FERN: Cross-Benchmark Table Retrieval for Text-to-SQL with Frozen Retrievers and Learned Ranking
items.description: Text-to-SQL systems over large pooled catalogs must first retrieve the tables a question needs. We compare against the published table recall of RASL, which uses Claude 3.5 models to extract keywords and select tables, on pooled BIRD, Spider, and Fiben catalogs. FERN (Feature-Engineered Ranking with No generative LLM) instead fuses three frozen retrievers into 100 candidates, describes each with up to 120 features, and reorders them with LightGBM rankers fitted once on BIRD's training questions.

items.description: Policy optimization is central to language model post-training, yet principled guidance remains limited. We revisit its theoretical foundations to identify algorithms that learn near-optimal policies using total samples and gradient steps governed by the base model's response coverage, a measure of how readily it generates optimal responses. Every observation influences the estimate in two roles, through its own evaluation when it is held out and through the models it helps fit when it trains. items.name: Accurate predictions of properties of energetic materials with tabular foundation models
items.title: Accurate predictions of properties of energetic materials with tabular foundation models
items.description: We use TabPFN, a recently developed tabular foundation model, to predict three properties of energetic materials: impact sensitivity, decomposition temperature and crystal density. Without any hyperparameter tuning, TabPFN outperforms the best published models for all three properties. items.name: When does text encoding matter for language modeling?
items.title: When does text encoding matter for language modeling?
items.description: UTF-8's role as the de facto encoding standard in language models introduces cross-lingual inequities due to its variable-length design. However, the effect that this encoding choice has on model performance remains largely unexamined. items.name: UGG: Unified Generative Geometry Model
items.title: UGG: Unified Generative Geometry Model
items.description: Understanding 4D scenes is a core challenge in visual intelligence, requiring models to jointly capture scene geometry, appearance, and dynamics from partial observations. However, existing approaches are subdivided into feedforward models for direct geometric prediction, and generative models for visual synthesis. items.name: One Policy for 100 Household Tasks: Our Solution for the 2026 BEHAVIOR Challenge
items.title: One Policy for 100 Household Tasks: Our Solution for the 2026 BEHAVIOR Challenge
items.description: We describe our solution for the 2026 BEHAVIOR Challenge: 100 long-horizon household tasks in the OmniGibson simulator. We placed 9th on the final leaderboard, the only independent team in the top 10. The core of the solution is a single vision-language-action (VLA) model, one checkpoint for all 100 tasks, built on our 1st-place 2025 solution, which is based on $π_{0.5}$. Although the two methods share fundamental search principles, their different ways of exploring the search space can lead to substantially different computational performance. items.title: Quantifying the Sampling Frequency Invariance of Time-Series Foundation Models for Sensor Data Applications
items.description: Time-Series Foundation Models (TSFMs) are increasingly used in sensor applications, where sampling frequency (SF) varies across sensors, devices, and operating modes (e.g., power saving). items.title: DnNP: Denoising Input Uncertainty in Neural Processes
items.description: Neural Processes (NPs) are flexible meta-learning models capable of uncertainty quantification across diverse applications. However, the standard NP framework assumes access to noise-free inputs. This is unrealistic in many practical settings, where sensor noise or measurement errors are unavoidable. items.name: Earlybird: Predictive Streaming Speech Recognition in 29M Parameters
items.title: Earlybird: Predictive Streaming Speech Recognition in 29M Parameters
items.description: Streaming speech recognizers output a word only after the speaker has finished it, typically 90-400 ms later. For a voice agent every millisecond counts: the sooner the words are outputted, the sooner the agent can start a search or plan its reply. items.description: Formal world models can support planning, verification, and safety reasoning, but constructing them from open-ended natural-language situations is difficult, particularly in multi-agent settings where several formalizations may be plausible.
